# Numbered Docs Chapters

Prose documentation is organised as a **numbered book**: `01-architecture.md`, `02-roadmap.md`,
`03-android-permissions-and-legal.md`, `04-accessibility-service.md`, an index README mapping each
chapter to what it covers, and a newest-first dated `CHANGELOG.md` alongside them.

[[farely]] is the only repository in the source set that applies numbering to *documents*. Elsewhere
the same instinct lands on directories of code — see [[numbered-stages-in-directory-names]], which
treats this as its prose variant.

## The division of labour

The four chapters divide by *question asked*, not by component: how it works, what is left to do, what
it is allowed to do, how the capture layer behaves. The CHANGELOG then carries everything time-shaped,
which keeps the chapters in the present tense. That separation is why the architecture chapter still
reads cleanly a month later while the roadmap moved constantly — see [[phase-status-board]].

The number is a **reading order**, not a dependency order. Chapter 01 is where a cold reader starts,
which makes this the same premise as [[readme-as-guided-tour]] applied one level down.

## Evidence

The chapters carry real argument, not summary. Chapter 01 states the reading strategy the whole
product depends on:

> "**Node tree before OCR.** OCR is the expensive, fragile path. Many Android apps expose offer text as
> real `TextView` nodes, readable in microseconds with no image processing. OCR is a fallback, not the
> default."
> — Farley/docs/ocr-overlay/01-architecture.md, 2026-07-02

And the index README, which should be the most stable file of the set, is the one that rotted:

> "**Phase 0 — Documentation.** No native code merged yet"
> — Farley/docs/ocr-overlay/README.md, 2026-07-02

That line still stands roughly **thirteen phases** behind `02-roadmap.md`.

## The failure mode the pattern invites

Numbering fixes the *order* of documents; it does nothing for their *currency*, and it adds a place
where staleness hides. A reader who trusts the index — the correct behaviour, since the index is what
the numbering advertises — is the reader most likely to be misled. This is the local shape of
[[documentation-drift]], and Farely's version is severe: the chapters describe ML Kit OCR as shipped
when it is a stub, and the numbering makes those documents look authoritative.

The mitigation the repo actually has is the **CHANGELOG**, which is append-only and therefore cannot
lie about the past even when the chapters lie about the present. Where the chapters and the changelog
disagree, the dated entries win. That is also how [[import-finished-work-into-git]] is recoverable
here at all: ten days of pre-git work exist only as changelog entries.
